chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from a group of his shaykhs, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Sayyar al-Mad'ani, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on one of three nights, Allah will forgive him what preceded of his sin and what followed.' I said: 'Which nights, may I be your ransom?' He said: 'The night of al-Fitr, the night of al-Adha, and the night of the middle of Sha'ban.'

key_terms.لَيْلَةُ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The night of the middle of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific nights for visiting Imam Husayn's grave to receive forgiveness of sins?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith emphasizes the immense spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s shrine during the three major Islamic festivals, a practice deeply rooted in Shia devotional culture. The promise of comprehensive forgiveness—covering both past and future sins—underscores the shrine as a locus of divine mercy, particularly during these auspicious times when the veil between the earthly and divine realms is considered thinnest.
